title: Disjoint intermediate-depth M5.5+ pairs gave a 50% larger-first share in 2013-2025, with wide uncertainty
abstract: We tested whether the larger event tends to occur first in intermediate-depth earthquake pairs. We used a fixed global ComCat snapshot. We matched events by shortest time gap before we compared magnitudes. Each event entered at most one pair. Both events had preferred magnitude at least 5.5, depth 70-300 km, separation at most 200 km in three dimensions, and a gap of 1 to below 30 days. Their magnitude difference was at least 0.5. In 2013-2025, the larger event came first in 11 of 22 pairs (50.0%). The conditional 95% year-bootstrap interval was 30.4% to 72.7%. The intermediate-minus-shallow contrast was -2.5 percentage points, with limits -21.4 to 20.2. We also report 2000-2012, deep events and six rule checks. Sparse pairs, mixed magnitude types, selected windows and block independence limit inference. This is a descriptive ordering test, not an estimate of caused aftershocks. Code, aggregate counts, provenance and audits are included. External event records are excluded.

display.caption: Larger-first shares for disjoint pairs. Bars give conditional 95% year-bootstrap intervals. Early means 2000-2012; later means 2013-2025.

citations.reason: Published shallow disjoint-pair method motivates the depth extension. We wrote new code and use the same external catalog snapshot.
